CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: China should immediately announce retaliatory tariffs on the remaining ~$75 billion of U.S. imports not yet covered, targeting politically sensitive sectors (agriculture, energy, autos) to maximize leverage in key U.S. swing states. Simultaneously, signal willingness to resume negotiations if the U.S. rolls back the May 2019 escalation, but do not offer unilateral concessions.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to China is HIGH (0.55). As of August 2019, the U.S. has already raised tariffs from 10% to 25% on $200 billion of Chinese goods (effective May 10, 2019), and Trump has called for tariffs on 'essentially all remaining imports from China, valued at approximately $300 billion' (Reuters timeline, May 10 entry; Fox Business). This threatens China's export economy and manufacturing employment in export hubs. The USC analysis notes the trade war is 'principally about the most important and potentially profitable industries of the future — AI, cloud computing, robotics, green tech,' meaning the dispute targets China's core industrial policy ambitions (Made in China 2025). White House adviser Kudlow acknowledged 'both sides will suffer,' confirming mutual economic damage. However, China has already retaliated on $110 billion of U.S. goods and has room to target remaining U.S. exports, particularly agriculture in Trump's political base. Senator Graham's admission that tariffs will cause 'short-term pain in America' reveals U.S. domestic vulnerability. The action_score of -1.0 (maximal retaliation) is justified because: (1) the U.S. escalation to 25% on $200B and threat of tariffs on all remaining imports leaves China little room for further concession without capitulating on core industrial policy; (2) retaliatory tariffs on U.S. farm and energy exports create political pressure on Trump ahead of the 2020 election cycle; (3) China's economy, while stressed, can absorb the shock better than the U.S. political cycle can absorb farm-belt discontent. Retaliation is the appropriate action level because this is a direct mirror response to the U.S. May escalation, not a new initiative.
